cards.title: Introduction to Python Data Types
cards.content:
Every value in Python has a specific data type. Since Python is dynamically typed, you don't need to explicitly declare types when creating variables.

x = 10  # x is an integer
y = "Hello"  # y is a string

cards.title: Sequence Types: Lists and Tuples
cards.content:
Sequence types allow you to store multiple items in a single variable.

  • Lists are mutable (changeable): my_list = [1, 2, 3]
  • Tuples are immutable (unchangeable): my_tuple = (1, 2, 3)

content.text: Lists in Python are _____, meaning their elements can be modified after creation, unlike tuples which are immutable.

cards.title: Match Python Syntax to Data Types
Dictionaries and Sets
cards.content:
Dictionaries store key-value pairs:

user = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}

Sets store unique, unordered items:

unique_numbers = {1, 2, 3, 3}  # results in {1, 2, 3}

cards.title: Type Casting and Conversion
cards.content:
You can convert between data types using built-in constructor functions like int(), float(), and str().

num_str = "123"
num_int = int(num_str)  # Converts string to integer
